prize_parts.citation: for the discovery of the neutrino mixing angle theta-13 through the disappearance of reactor antineutrinos, by the Daya Bay and RENO experiments

statement.case_for: I have listened to the whole first round, and my preferred configuration is unchanged: a single part, B024, for the reactor measurement of theta-13. The case is a discovery about nature that could not have been deduced. Before 2012 theta-13 could have been tiny, in which case leptonic CP violation and the mass ordering would have been out of practical reach. Daya Bay's 5.2 sigma disappearance signal, followed within weeks by RENO, showed an angle of about nine degrees. That one number is why DUNE, Hyper-Kamiokande and JUNO exist in the form they do, and the result has been refined for over a decade inside a stable three-flavour picture. Nobody in round 1, including those who do not support B024, challenges its maturity. The 2015 prize rewarded the discovery that neutrinos oscillate and therefore have mass. It did not determine the mixing angles, and the size of theta-13 was an open and consequential question. I would give that as the distinction in the citation. I have narrowed the citation to Daya Bay and RENO, the two experiments that made the decisive measurement, and I accept that this explicitly leaves Double Chooz and the accelerator appearance results as precursors and cross-checks.
statement.case_against: The weaknesses are now clearer to me after the chair's questions. First, credit: Olsson's test, that we must be sure we have identified the people who did the original work, is harder for a three-spokesperson award from several-hundred-member collaborations than for two named inventors of a clock, and I cannot document each individual's decisive role beyond my memory that Luk and Wang led Daya Bay and Kim led RENO. Second, overlap with the 2015 prize: I find the distinction convincing, but several colleagues (Eriksson, Kroll, Pearce, Johansson) read theta-13 as a parameter of an already honoured framework, and that is a legitimate reading of how the public will see it. Third, breadth: only Pearce and I ranked it highly, and Pearce discloses a field affinity. Fourth, B049 has far broader support and its credit is cleaner, so if the committee cannot settle the attribution I should be ready to accept B049 and not hold out for my own preference.

responses.point: Johansson asked whether Daya Bay and RENO are a separate advance from the 2015 prize and whether Double Chooz leadership can be left out, noting that B024 deserves discussion and that attribution looks harder than for the clocks.
responses.response: I think they are a separate advance. The 2015 prize established that flavour oscillation occurs, which was the discovery that mattered most for the mass question. Theta-13 is a different measurement: before 2012 the third mixing angle was unknown and might have been vanishingly small, and its value decides whether CP violation in the lepton sector can be searched for at all. On Double Chooz, it reported the first indication in late 2011 at low significance and was overtaken by Daya Bay and RENO, whose 2012 results were each beyond five sigma or close to it; a citation tied to those two experiments can leave Double Chooz out without falsifying the history, though I would want the committee to say so openly. I will concede that this makes the credit narrower than my round-1 phrasing implied, and that it is exactly the kind of judgement that is easier for the clock.

responses.point: Olsson says her difficulty with B024 is attribution rather than merit: three spokespersons for near-simultaneous experiments may not meet the committee's test of identifying the people who did the original work, and she will consider it if the trio is shown to be uncontroversial.
responses.response: I cannot show you that from the supplied material, and I will not pretend otherwise. What I can say is that Luk and Wang were the Daya Bay co-spokespersons who led the 2012 analysis and Kim led RENO, and that these are the names most often attached to the discovery in the community. That is a statement about leadership, which is not the same as individual authorship, and your rule asks for more than that. I therefore regard the attribution as the real weak point of B024 and not as something I can argue away. If the committee shares your doubt, that is a better reason to move away from B024 than the 2015 overlap, and I would then prefer a clean two-name B049 to an uncertain three-name neutrino prize.

responses.point: Kroll asked how I rank the novelty of theta-13 against the clock and argues that the clock has a broader effect on other fields, while conceding that B024 is a strong and well-measured result.
responses.response: On novelty I still put theta-13 higher, because it is a measured fact about nature that changed what an entire programme looks for, whereas the clock so far reports a better number and null results on constants. I do not dismiss the breadth argument. Geodesy at the centimetre scale and dark-matter couplings are real downstream uses. But I notice that your own caveat, that the scientific harvest of the clock is partly prospective, is the same as mine, and that nothing in this exchange has changed my view that a prize should follow a discovery. If the clock delivers a surprise I would revise sharply; if the committee decides that a new regime of control of many atoms is itself the discovery, I can live with that, which is why B049 is now my first alternative.

responses.point: Pearce proposes B049 plus B047 with Halzen alone and says B047 would be dropped if his decisive role cannot be documented; he keeps B024 as an alternative but finds its argument for distinctness harder than for the clocks.
responses.response: I agree with the fallback you give yourself: B047 with one name for a collaboration of hundreds is the weakest part of any configuration on the table, and I do not support it as a second part. I rank it below where I put it in round 1, and I have removed it from my alternatives. The diffuse flux is secure, but the source identifications rest on one instrument, and I said last time I would wait for firmer evidence. A two-part prize also forces a choice between credit lists that cannot be balanced with three names. On B024 versus the clock, I accept that your distinctness argument cuts in both directions and that the clock has the cleaner credit. I disagree only that the clock's discovery content is yet established.

responses.point: Eriksson argues that B048 opened a new class of states of matter, whereas theta-13 is a parameter of an established framework, and that the 2015 prize makes B024 more of a follow-on.
responses.response: I accept the weighting argument for B048 in principle, since a new symmetry class with protected edge states is a more conceptual advance than fixing an angle. My view is that the angle was not a foregone conclusion and its being large was a surprise. Where I side with you is that B048 is the strongest condensed-matter fallback, and I keep it as an alternative. I would still ask you to address the HgTe question honestly: until the edge conductance has been reproduced widely outside Molenkamp's group and the Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang prediction is acknowledged, I find the credit more compromised than you do.

uncertainties: Whether Luk, Kim and Wang can be defended as the credited people for Daya Bay and RENO; I rely on memory for individual roles and the committee has no source to settle it in this discussion.
Whether the committee accepts that theta-13 is a distinct discovery from the 2015 oscillation prize.
Whether B049 is a discovery-class result or an instrument achievement, and whether a measured departure (constants drift, time dilation) might change that in the next few years.
Whether the exclusion of Double Chooz and the accelerator appearance results is acceptable to the committee.
statement.conflict_note: I have no conflict with any shortlisted candidate. David Gross, Thomas Van Riet and the Uppsala string group are not connected to them. I am a theorist outside every shortlisted field and defer to specialists on technical detail. I note Pearce's disclosed field affinity for B024 and B047 and Johansson's flagged bias on B038 and B044; neither changes my own assessment, which I held before reading them.
